Starting values for a gcTMB model

Source: R/gcTMBstart.R
gcTMBstart.Rd

Computes starting values for the fixed-effect parameters of a growth curve, which can be inspected, modified, and passed to the start argument of gcTMB.

Usage

gcTMBstart(
  form,
  fform = NULL,
  data,
  start = NULL,
  fix = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  family = "gaussian",
  model = "logistic",
  truncated = TRUE,
  link = NULL,
  b1type = c("asymptote", "rate"),
  method = "lm",
  gsl = NULL,
  gsu = NULL,
  gsn = NULL
)

Arguments

form

Formula, with the names of the response and the time variable, e.g. weight ~ day

fform

Formula, list of formulas, or NULL. Fixed effects for the model parameters: a formula of the form b1 + b2 ~ Treatment, or a list of such formulas, e.g. list(b1 ~ Treatment, b2 ~ Treatment + Site). Parameters not listed have a single intercept (~ 1). A list of five right-hand side formulas, one for each of b1-b5 (X1 = ~ 1, ..., X5 = ~ 1), is also accepted.

data

Data frame. Observations with missing values in the variables of the model or in the weights are left out.

start

Numeric vector or NULL. Starting values for each model parameter. Only NA entries are replaced.

fix

Logical vector or NULL. A vector with the same length as start. If TRUE, a model coefficient is fixed to the starting value. The threshold b4 and the asymmetry b5 are fixed by default, at 0 and 1 unless given in start; fix=c(b4=FALSE) or fix=c(b5=FALSE) estimates them. Without truncation, b4 is not used and always fixed, at 0 unless given in start.

weights

Numeric vector or NULL. Weights, one for each row of data.

family

Character string. The distribution of the response, see gcTMB.

model

Character string. The growth model: "logistic", "gompertz", "hill", "weibull", "normal", "gamma" or "linear", see gcTMB.

truncated

Logical. If TRUE (default), the curve is truncated at a threshold b4, by default fixed at 0, see gcTMB.

link

Named character vector or NULL. Links of the parameters b1-b5, see gcTMB.

b1type

Character string. The meaning of b1, "asymptote" (default) or "rate" for the maximum growth rate, see gcTMB.

method

Character string. One of "lm" or "grid".

gsl

Numeric vector or NULL. Lower bounds for the grid search, same length as start, on the scale of the coefficients (the rate 1/b3 for b3 with the inverse link); NA (or NULL) for the default range.

gsu

Numeric vector or NULL. Upper bounds for the grid search, same length as start; NA (or NULL) for the default range.

gsn

Integer, a single number or a vector, or NULL. Number of grid points for each parameter, a single number or a vector with the same length as start (default 10). A parameter with gsn = 1 stays at its "lm" starting value.

Value

A named numeric vector of starting values, one for each model coefficient.

Details

Method "lm" linearises the growth curve: for a given asymptote b1, the mean response at each time t, relative to b1, gives Finv(y/b1) = z(t), with the inverse Finv of the function F of the model (qlogis for logistic and hill, -log(-log(q)) for gompertz, log(-log(1 - q)) for weibull) and the transformed time z(t) (see gcTMB), which is linear in the time t (logistic, gompertz) or in log(t) (hill, weibull). A linear regression of Finv(y/b1) on t or log(t) gives b2 and b3 from its intercept and slope, e.g. b3 as the inverse of the slope and b2 as the time at which the line crosses zero for the logistic model; with b2 or b3 given in start, only the other one is estimated. The weibull shape b3 starts at least at 1.1. The observed responses often do not reach the asymptote yet, so b1 is profiled: for asymptotes from just above the largest mean response to four times it, the linearised fit gives b2 and b3, b1 is refitted by least squares for this curve, and the asymptote with the smallest residual sum of squares is used. Mean responses below 1\ linearised curve and are left out. With covariates in fform, the pooled starting value of each parameter is projected onto its design matrix, giving the intercept or each group the pooled value and contrasts a value of zero. The threshold b4, fixed at 0 by default, starts when estimated where the curve without truncation reaches 1\ time with a positive count, and for the lognormal and beta families before all times, as positive responses are impossible before the threshold. The asymmetry b5 starts at 1, the symmetric curve, with which b2 and b3 are linearised unless b5 is given in start; b4 without truncation starts at 0.

Method "grid" evaluates the negative log-likelihood (without random effects) at all combinations of a grid of parameter values and returns the best grid point; parameters not included in the grid start at the values of method "lm". Without bounds in gsl and gsu, default ranges are used for b2 (the time range extended by a quarter at both ends, positive with the log link) and b3 (1/4 to 4 times its "lm" starting value, log-spaced; on the scale of its link). Default ranges are only used for parameters with a single coefficient in fform; the asymptote b1 is only included in the grid with user-specified bounds.

Examples

gcTMBstart(height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, model="gompertz")
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b4:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>      131.87454       27.92580       19.32536        0.00000        1.00000 
# with a given asymptote, from which b2 and b3 are linearised
gcTMBstart(height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, start=c(b1=120))
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b4:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>      120.00000       33.47664       11.57527        0.00000        1.00000 
# best point of a grid of b2 and b3 values
gcTMBstart(height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, method="grid", gsn=c(1, 10, 10, 1, 1))
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b4:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>     118.820547      33.583333       9.643623       0.000000       1.000000
